messages.subject: count events with stochastic mapping
parts:
Hi  Nick,

Actually I am working on the historical biogeography of a group of plants along the Andes and in addition to the ancestral range reconstruction I am interested to count biogeographical event s over time and in the different clades.  I calculated the stochastic mapping simulations following the instructions in “running_stochastic_mapping_stratified_v1.R”  but  I don’t know how to get the mean and variance of the counts of each event type. I was checking the “master_table_cladogenetic_events” and the “resmod” objects but I don’t find the way.  I’d like to extract  an output as you present in the example with the count of the  anagenetic and cladogenetic events…

==========================================

Biogeographical stochastic mapping event counts, 100 realizations on Psychotria (19 taxa, 4 areas, M0 unconstrained)

 

Mean of event counts:

       d        e        a        y        s        v        j

5.527778 1.629630 0.000000 9.842593 3.444444 4.712963 0.000000

 

Standard deviation of event counts:

        d         e         a         y         s         v         j

0.8367531 1.0987894 0.0000000 1.5234125 1.4997404 0.8652257 0.0000000

==========================================

  

Thank you very much and best wishes!!!

diego

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: count events with stochastic mapping
parts:
Hi!  Once you have the master_table_cladogenetic_events, you should be able to just summarize that table in various routine R ways -- e.g.:

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/9847054/how-to-get-summary-statistics-by-group

...I think I do this in the script somewhere but I forget.  As previously mentioned stochastic mapping is "beta" and needs more checking, documentation, and example/accessory scripts, but the basic results look reasonable...

Nick
